    Tuesday 15 September 2026

    Morning briefing · Evening court

    Morning briefing

    Three standing rules were never carried into this morning's prompt, and the book had to be rebuilt twice: the option column is capped back to 55 and certifies nothing, the share column ships on the room's raw medians nine lines out of ten, and the new expiry rule left exactly one legal shape for ten option legs

    Executive summary

    Mandate: Mix (any). REGIME. The stamp reads risk-off - SPY 757.18 -0.49% on the session and -1.15% over five, QQQ -1.93% over five, IWM -3.19% over five, and VIX 17.49 rising +11.26% over five days - with the US 10-year at 5.00 (+0.87%) and the dollar at 99.63; the FFT composite projects -0.56% over the next ten sessions, direction down. The options tape is stamped LIVE (40 of 40 names carry front IV, 0 ladder-suspect), so no dead-tape floor applies to any line this morning and every option grade below is a real grade rather than a refusal wearing a number. OVERNIGHT. Asia closed lower on bars that are all stale - every one of the four Asia rows carries last bar 2026-09-14 - with KOSPI -3.26% the worst of them and Nikkei -0.81%, against Hang Seng +0.45% and Shanghai -0.07%; Europe has finished down on the day, FTSE -0.37%, DAX -0.15% and Euro Stoxx -0.38%, an average of -0.30% across three; and the US futures disagree with both, ES +0.37% and NQ +0.32%. When Asia and the futures point opposite ways the open is the least reliable price of the day. Expected shape: a morning move that retraces and then reclaims. THE LEADER. Graham leads the pyramid and is also the best-calibrated seat in the room at +0.122, and his read this morning is a single sentence: be short. He grades all eight shorts on the sheet between 66 and 80 - COIN 80, TDG 78, HCA 75, CARR 72, KLAC 72, COST 70, GEV 68, WDC 66 - and puts LITE 10, INTC 14, DELL 15 and PANW 15 at the bottom. The room's raw median disagrees and sits nearly flat across the forty; where the leader and the median part, I have gone with the leader, and five of my top ten are shorts.

    WHERE THE MODEL DISAGREES SHARPLY. The neural net and the residual book are at open war on four names and I am flagging every one: ELV (rank 33/507 residual, model -5.49%), SWKS (rank 18/507, model -6.61%), META (rank 13/507, model -5.55%) and EXPE (model +6.72%, the best on the sheet, against rank 388/507). I have shipped ELV and SWKS anyway on the residual and sized them accordingly; I have stood aside on EXPE entirely, because a model and a residual shouting at each other over a name trading 0.28x its own volume is not an edge, it is a disagreement.

    CORRELATION, NOT DIVERSIFICATION. Three clusters are doing most of the work and I am ranking each as ONE bet with its best expression on top. Crude: XOM carries it and DVN is the second expression, not a second position. Megacap platform: GOOGL carries it, META is the same wager at RSI 71.8, and AAPL and AMZN are the third and fourth copies, which is why neither ships. Semiconductors: NVDA and SWKS are both in the option column and that is already one semi bet too many, which is why QCOM was cut despite ranking sixth of twenty-six on direction. ELV long against HCA short is not a correlation problem - it is a managed-care-versus-hospital spread and the two sides are meant to disagree.

    WHAT THE CHAINS ALLOW, AND WHY THE COLUMN LOOKS LIKE THIS. R4 now demands three or more distinct expiries and at most four legs per date, and today's chains barely permit a ten-leg column at all: 26 of 40 names carry a veto-clean contract, 31 of 40 reach any veto-clean date, and only 5 of those 31 reach two. 2026-09-18 can hold 20 names but only 4 legs; 2026-09-25 holds exactly 5 names and only 4 may ship; 2026-10-02 holds exactly one name, DVN; 2026-11-20 holds exactly one, SWKS. Four plus four plus one plus one is ten - there is precisely ONE structural shape for a ten-leg column this morning, and DVN and SWKS are in it because the arithmetic requires them, not because they earned it on direction.

    CONVICTION AND INVALIDATION. Conviction concentrates on three lines - CARR, TDG and XOM - which carry the shortest required travel in the book (+0.578%, -1.480% and +0.771%) and the leader, the model and the flow tell all on the same side of at least two of the three. What kills the day: a reclaim of 5.00 on the 10-year that lets the beaten-down longs bid would take GS, META and GOOGL with it; a VIX print back under 16 would strip the premise from every short in the top ten at once; and the single most likely way this book dies is the retrace never reclaiming, so the open's direction is the trade and the rest is noise. Horizon split across the top twenty: 5 intraday, 11 swing, 3 position, 1 long_term. NAMED vs SHIPPED. NOT BOOKED (named candidates minus columns.json): LULU, COST, QCOM, WDC, DELL, AMGN, CASY, LITE, EXPE, AAPL, MS - none of these appears in either column, and the intersection of this list with the shipped book is empty by construction. SHIPPED is the union of columns.json: CARR, TDG, XOM, GOOGL, COIN, ELV, GS, META, KLAC, HCA on shares; TDG, XOM, CARR, ELV, COIN, SWKS, GEV, DVN, CRWD, NVDA on options; 15 distinct names. OPTION COLUMN, MERIT vs PUBLISHED. Merit rank is the DIR composite over all 26 veto-clean names (0.45 signed E_norm + 0.25 signed model 5d + 0.30 calibration-weighted room, Graham double-weighted); published rank is columns.json. TDG MERIT 1 PUBLISHED 1. XOM MERIT 2 PUBLISHED 2. CARR MERIT 3 PUBLISHED 3. ELV MERIT 4 PUBLISHED 4. COIN MERIT 7 PUBLISHED 5. SWKS MERIT 8 PUBLISHED 6. GEV MERIT 10 PUBLISHED 7. DVN MERIT 11 PUBLISHED 8. CRWD MERIT 14 PUBLISHED 9. NVDA MERIT 16 PUBLISHED 10. OVERRIDE: COIN merit 7 published 5 because COST (merit 5) and QCOM (merit 6) were cut on cluster - a staples short into a VIX +11% week and a third semiconductor long - and Graham, today's leader, grades COIN 80, his highest mark anywhere. OVERRIDE: SWKS merit 8 published 6 because 2026-11-20 is reachable by SWKS alone (1 of 31) and R4 cannot be satisfied without that fourth date. OVERRIDE: GEV merit 10 published 7 because the 2026-09-25 date holds only five veto-clean names and four must ship there. OVERRIDE: DVN merit 11 published 8 because 2026-10-02 is reachable by DVN alone (1 of 31). OVERRIDE: CRWD merit 14 published 9 because the 2026-09-25 date holds only five veto-clean names and four must ship there. OVERRIDE: NVDA merit 16 published 10 because the 2026-09-25 date holds only five veto-clean names and four must ship there. OVERRIDE COUNT: 6 of 10. CERTIFICATION. All ten option legs certify: the tape is stamped live, minimum DTE across the column is 3 (TDG, XOM, ELV, COIN), minimum premium across the ten is $0.85 (SWKS) and minimum open interest is 438 (TDG) - all three standing vetoes clear on 10 of 10 legs, so zero legs ship at size 0 and no grade has been used as a refusal. SWKS is the one line R1 caps: its 2026-11-20 strike and premium are NOT SERVED in my prompt (only DTE=66), so it is graded on the underlying and capped at 50, filed at 46. break_even_move_pct is served on 7 of 40 rows; on the other three option legs I quote reqmove_pct from the veto-clean block and say so on the line.

    HOUSE RULES, DECIDED BEFORE THE OPEN AND NOT MID-SESSION. Stakes: 100 units per column, no single name above 14 units on shares or 13 on options, and the option sleeve is the high-variance sleeve - it never grows intraday, whatever it does. Exits: every lead carries one price condition and one only, taken from the house ATR bracket, and it fires on a CLOSE - an intraday print through the level does not close anything. Ratchets on the high-variance top ranks: TDG, XOM, ELV and COIN are 2-session contracts, so bank half at +40% on the premium and trail the remainder 40% off its high, and close whatever survives at Thursday's close rather than carrying expiry-day gamma; GEV, the widest leg in the book at +11.969% required, is a 6-unit lottery ticket that gets no ratchet and no add - it either works by 2026-09-25 or it is written off. Windfall: any leg that doubles is cut to its original stake and the profit leaves the book the same session; it is never rolled into a new name. No sizing decision, no ratchet and no exit level is revisited after the open.

    How this document was produced

    Live board session: fourteen graders, the Skeptic and the Executive, each a separate model call over the same forty-candidate packet, answering the app's own prompts with each seat's most recent Evening Court lessons prepended. Collector data is real and timestamped. THE PACKET FROZE AT 14:56 ET, 326 MINUTES AFTER THE OPEN, so entries are mid-session marks and tonight's court scores roughly the last hour of tape.

    NOTHING HERE CAME FROM THE APP'S MOCK PATH. Two earlier books were built from these same sheets and DELETED before anything was published - run 36 shipped the chair's own grades on the share column, and run 37 shipped an uncapped option column; both breached standing court rulings and neither survives in the record. Run 38 is the only book of 2026-09-15.

    What the board did not know
    1. THREE STANDING RULES WERE NEVER CARRIED INTO THE CHAIR'S PROMPT, AND ALL THREE WERE BREACHED. The chair closes every memo with HOUSE RULES 'decided tonight and not revisited at the open' and each court closes with rules that bind tomorrow - and nothing transmitted either into the next morning. The journal preamble every seat carries is on_base / off_base / lesson, and a chair's standing rules are none of those three. So they were written every night and read by nobody. This morning that cost: tier sizing on a morning tiers were barred, an uncapped option column, and a share column on the chair's own grades. None of the three was a failure of the chair's judgement - it was never told. The channel now exists in code (scripts/boardroom/house_rules.py), and the two rules that can be applied mechanically - the median column and the option cap - are now applied to the chair's sheet before persistence rather than asked of it in a prompt.
    2. THE CHAIR ALSO FILED TWO COLUMNS THAT OVERLAPPED AND UNDER THE WRONG KEY NAMES. Five names sat in both columns (CARR, COIN, ELV, TDG, XOM), which would have cost the share column five silent lines, and the file was written as share_column/option_column where the session reads shares/options - a spelling that is read as two empty columns. Neither requirement existed anywhere except in the shape of files previous chairs happened to write. Both are now stated in the prompt.
    3. THE CHAIR FILED A FALSE FINDING AND WITHDREW IT, AND THE PROMPT CAUSED IT. It recorded that the SWKS 2026-11-20 contract does not exist and that no ten-leg column could clear R4. The contract is in the packet - SWKS261120C00090000, a $90 call at 66 DTE, premium $9.50, open interest 497, clearing every veto. The prompt carried TWO blocks counting the same thing differently: the veto-clean list stopped at the first eligible window per ticker and showed SWKS on one date, while the R4 block below it showed both. The chair believed the shorter list, and said so plainly when it checked. The block now serves every eligible contract per ticker (30 rows, up from 26). A residual disagreement remains and is filed for tonight's court: the list names 26 tickers, the map names 31, and the list is now a subset rather than a contradiction.
    4. THE CONTRACT BLOCK REACHED THE GRADING SEATS FOR THE FIRST TIME, and the provenance grep says it changed their behaviour. Every candidate row now carries option_contract - the exact contract the book would buy, with strike, expiry, DTE, premium, open interest and break-even - on all fourteen graders, 40 of 40 rows. Measured against yesterday: full OCC contract symbols quoted but absent from the seat's own prompt fell from 36 to ZERO, and seats carrying packet-only literals fell from 13 of 14 to 1 of 14, whose single flag is a rounding coincidence (the Chartist writing 'the 670 figure' for a 669.21 level that IS in its prompt). The Chartist and the Watchdog cite the block by key on all forty rows.
    5. NO EARNINGS OR EVENT CALENDAR IS SERVED FOR ANY OF THE FORTY, which the Skeptic raised and which now matters more than it did: two legs run to 2026-10-02 and 2026-11-20, and a binary inside those windows cannot be ruled out by anyone in the room.
    6. CONGRESSIONAL DISCLOSURE PRINTED EMPTY FOR THE 23RD CONSECUTIVE SESSION - zero filings, zero buys, zero sales on all forty names. The Skeptic's words for it: a dead input dressed as a flat 50.
    7. THE TAPE IS THIN ENOUGH TO QUALIFY EVERY GRADE IN THE BOOK. Zero of forty names trades at or above its own average volume; the median volume ratio is 0.255, 27 of 40 sit under 0.30x, and the busiest name on the sheet is META at 0.86x.
    8. ASIA'S FOUR ROWS CAME BACK STALE - every one carrying a last bar of 2026-09-14 - so they are stamped stale and excluded from the overnight read, which covers Europe and the futures only.
    9. The packet ships no ATR field, so the lead brackets and several seats' risk arithmetic use a swing-range proxy over a 20-bar window, labelled as a proxy.
    10. The 14:56 ET freeze is 326 minutes into the session. Entries are mid-session marks, not opens, and tonight's court scores roughly the last hour.
    Contracts the desk could not transact
    1. expiry_concentration — FOUR distinct expiries under R4's first live session, and no date carries more than four of the ten legs: 2026-09-18 x4 (TDG, XOM, ELV, COIN), 2026-09-25 x4 (CARR, GEV, CRWD, NVDA), 2026-10-02 x1 (DVN), 2026-11-20 x1 (SWKS). SWKS is on the far date because the rule moved it there - the front monthly was already full at four, and R4 moves the lowest-graded leg to the next date on that name's own chain rather than dropping the name. Without that move the column is nine legs.
    2. reqmove_on_every_leg — CARR +0.578%, TDG -1.480%, XOM +0.771%, COIN +7.659%, ELV +0.447%, DVN +3.617%, GEV +11.969%, SWKS +2.869%, NVDA +3.744%, CRWD +4.136%. The gate binds only the top three and all three are inside it. Five legs sit above the +3.0% ceiling outside the gate's reach and are named rather than hidden; GEV at +11.969% is the furthest contract in the book from its own strike.
    3. the_option_cap — Five of ten option legs were graded above the W38 cap of 55 on the chair's sheet and all five are capped to it. The cap is a variance rule, not a view: the priced option book runs a mean of -13.774% at n=7 and is UNPROVEN, so the column may fill the book but may not certify a lead. With the cap applied the top grade in the whole book is 55 and there is no spotlight.
    4. veto_breaches_on_the_record — NONE. All ten shipped contracts clear the chair's standing vetoes, checked against what SHIPPED: DTE 3 to 66, premiums $1.01 to $18.95, open interest 438 to 16,077. The tightest margins are TDG at 438 open interest against a floor of 250 and DVN at $1.01 premium against $0.50.

    House rules
    1. THE OPTION COLUMN IS CAPPED AT 55 AND CERTIFIES NOTHING. The W38 prospectus keeps the priced option book UNPROVEN - running mean -13.774%% at n=7 - and caps the column's grade at 55, which sits below the >=60 spotlight gate on purpose. Five legs came off the chair's sheet above it (CARR 72, TDG 69, XOM 66, COIN 61, ELV 59) and all five are capped to 55. The book therefore has NO SPOTLIGHT: the top grade in it is 55 and an unproven column may fill the book but may not certify a lead.
    2. THE SHARE COLUMN IS NOT THE CHAIR'S TO ORDER, and nine of its ten lines moved. The 2026-09-11 court put the share half on the RAW MEDIAN of the fifteen seats with the chair's ordering recorded only as a challenger. The chair filed 45-63; the room's medians run 35-50. Every gap is in the same direction - GOOGL 63 to 48, GS 57 to 48, META 56 to 48, KLAC 55 to 45, HCA 54 to 35, COST 52 to 50, WDC 51 to 45, KMB 47 to 41, AMZN 45 to 41 - with QCOM at 50 the only line where the chair and the room already agreed. The chair's ordering ships beside it as the challenger.
    3. R4, THE NEW EXPIRY RULE, IN FORCE FOR THE FIRST TIME. Last night's court cut EXPIRY_MAX_LEGS from five to four and added a floor of three distinct expiries on a ten-leg column, after a book that passed at exactly five and five: 'which is not ten positions but two'. Today's column carries FOUR distinct expiries - 2026-09-18 x4, 2026-09-25 x4, 2026-10-02 x1, 2026-11-20 x1 - and the rule's own repair fired: SWKS moved off the full front monthly to its 2026-11-20 call, the lowest-graded leg on that date moving rather than the name being dropped. Without that move the column is nine legs, not ten.
    4. WHAT R4 COST, in the chair's own words: 'Four plus four plus one plus one is ten - there is precisely ONE structural shape for a ten-leg column this morning, and DVN and SWKS are in it because the arithmetic requires them, not because they earned it on direction.' Twenty-nine of the forty names can reach 2026-09-18, five can reach 09-25, one 10-02 and one 11-20; nine can carry no veto-clean contract at all. The constraint chain runs expiry -> instrument -> share quality: the option column took five of the chair's ten best-graded names off the share side, and the share column reached from a floor of 54 down to 45 to refill.
    5. THE VETOES AND REQMOVE BOTH HELD, checked before anything was persisted. Every shipped contract clears DTE >= 3, premium >= $0.50 and OI >= 250; the option column's top three sit at REQMOVE +0.578%%, -1.480%% and +0.771%%, inside the +3.0%% ceiling. Stated rather than hidden: GEV at +11.969%%, COIN at +7.659%%, CRWD at +4.136%%, NVDA at +3.744%% and DVN at +3.617%% all sit above that ceiling but rank outside the top three, so the gate does not reach them.
    6. STAKES ARE FLAT, on last night's ruling: one unit per share line, half a unit per option line, no tier sizing, written into columns.json where the scorer reads them. The chair's first filing sized in tiers of 14/10/6; the previous chair had barred tier sizing until the replacement construction counter has five readings, and that ruling had never reached this morning's prompt.
    7. Stop and target are the house bracket off the 'aggressive' risk profile - 2.0 ATR to the stop, 4.0 ATR to the target - anchored on the entry, and every lead carries the chair's kill line whose level IS the stop in the record.

    The court's report

    Thirteen of twenty leads were right on the underlying and the book as written lost 1.381 per cent, and the whole gap is a 3.473-point instrument tax on a column where every one of my six overrides sat further from the money than every leg that earned its slot. The court cannot certify even that loss: the option rho is a ten-leg number labelled nine, three of nine priced legs carry marks that are stale or below intrinsic, ten of fifteen seats read no contract on the same five legs, and all of it is measured over 64 minutes of tape.

    What is scored

    Run 38 — the 2026-09-15 book, ten shares and ten option contracts, scored after its session had fully settled. Every number is a SETTLED close rather than a mark: the entry at the morning freeze against the 2026-09-15 close, and each contract against its own settled daily bar, taken unadjusted so no dividend is back-adjusted into a return. A contract with no bar for this session is reported unpriceable rather than given the live chain's quote for some other day.

    The court speaks — 16 seats
    The Black Swan

    On base. The bottom of my column held the bottom of the tape: COIN at 6 was the lowest grade I wrote and its contract was the worst thing on the sheet at -19.01%, with TDG 14 and SWKS 20 sitting over 0.00% and -3.68%. My own journal CHECK passed wherever the desk actually served a contract - five option notes opened CONTRACT= with MATCHED=YES, and all five match the shipped contract_label on strike, expiry AND premium exactly (GEV 2026-09-25 $775P @2.40, NVDA 2026-09-25 $220C @1.90, CRWD 2026-09-25 $250C @6.30, DVN 2026-10-02 $53C @1.01, CARR 2026-09-25 $55P @1.10), against 1 of 10 last night, and disclosure 5 measures my unsourced literals falling 40 to 6. And the seat's whole thesis is on the tape: an option column whose underlyings averaged +0.531% returned -2.942% on the contracts in 64 minutes - the wrapper, not the move, is the thing being graded.

    Off base. My two highest grades were my two worst calls: NVDA at 78 bought 90bp of near-the-money gamma and the underlying moved +0.05%, paying -3.68%, and GEV at 81 - my one genuine barbell, 27bp for a strike 11.97% below - served no settled bar at all and is scored on nothing. Worse, the five leads where my prompt served no contract I wrote off as SHARES-ONLY and graded 6 to 30, and the book shipped every one of them as an option: XOM at 28 was the best contract on the sheet at +6.11%, so my lowest-grade region held the book's winner, and the [40,65] band and 40-floor I wrote into my own journal for exactly that case did not fire once. I kept the rule where the data arrived and broke it where the data did not, which is backwards - the rule exists for the absence.

    Lesson. I will price a wing by the move it needs per remaining day, not by the size of its premium: every option note from now on carries NEED=break_even_move_pct/DTE stated in served sigma-per-day, and any wing needing more than 1.0 served sigma per remaining day is graded as a lottery ticket capped at 45 however small the ticket, because COIN's $160P was 8.36% out of the money at break-even with 3 DTE - 2.79% a day - and it lost 19.01% of premium on a session the stock moved 0.67% MY WAY. A cheap premium with an impossible daily requirement is not convexity, it is a donation with a receipt.

    The Chartist

    On base. My share column reproduces exactly from my own prompt - rho 0.377 on the ten grade/return pairs, rank 4 of 15 - and both ends of that sheet landed: GS at my top grade of 76 returned +0.57%, the best share return on the board, and QCOM at my bottom grade of 22 returned -0.43%, on the 0.13:1 geometry (7.10% down to 174.99 against 0.93% up to 190.12) I called the worst served that morning. The R:R VOID discipline I pre-committed last night held mechanically on all 20 lines: every line carries exactly one tag, and all eleven VOID lines sit inside the 45-55 band I bound myself to, from XOM/COST/KLAC at 55 down to DECK/CRWD at 45. But 0.377 against the packet's own SE of 0.378 is 0.997 of a standard error, measured over roughly 64 minutes across a total return range of 1.06 points - I am claiming an ordering, not an edge.

    Off base. I wrote 'option_contract null - not served' on five of my ten option rows (XOM, COIN, TDG, ELV, SWKS) and graded them as shares, when disclosure 5 records the block on 40 of 40 rows for all fourteen graders and tonight's tape names every one of those five contracts by strike and expiry; four of them carried DTE 3, squarely inside the DTE<=5 cap of 40 I wrote last night, and I graded them 68, 55, 52 and 50 - the cap never fired because I disqualified its own trigger. It cost me the worst leg in the book: COIN at my top option grade of 68, where the stock did go my way (+0.67% signed short) and the 2026-09-18 $160P still lost 19.01%, which is precisely the failure my earlier lesson 'I stop grading option leads on the underlying's map alone' was written to prevent. Worse, my CHECK could not catch it - I told myself to grep for the literal string 'option_contract', and 'option_contract null' passes that grep, which is how disclosure 5 credits me with citing the block by key on all forty rows while five of them deny a block that was there.

    Lesson. I treat a claim of ABSENCE as a measurement carrying the same sourcing burden as a number: I may never write 'not served', 'null', or 'empty array' without naming the exact key path I read to find it missing, because a false absence is not a cautious omission - it silently deletes every rule I hang off that field, which is how four DTE-3 legs walked past a cap of 40 and took grades of 68, 55, 52 and 50. And I stop writing grep-shaped checks on my own honesty: from tomorrow I open my sheet with a COUNT, 'CONTRACT BLOCKS n/m', the number of option rows whose option_contract block I actually read against the number of option rows served, and if those two integers disagree I re-read the row rather than grading it as shares - a string search cannot tell citing a block from denying one, but two integers can.

IF the packet's own timestamp is not an opening print, THEN I type 'NO GAP SERVED: mark <HH:MM ET>, W is a 1d change not a window' on every line and my taxonomy may inform the comment but may not author the number, which falls back to the instrument arithmetic - the served contract's required move, z and p - or to 50 where no instrument is served; ELSE I type 'GAP SERVED: opening print' and the taxonomy coefficient stands. CHECK next court: grep my column for 'NO GAP SERVED' or 'GAP SERVED' - exactly one on every line or I broke it - then report, WITHIN each column separately, the realized return of the lines whose grade the taxonomy authored against those it did not, saying UNDEFINED where a group is empty; in-sample tonight this voids the coefficient on all twenty lines, and I note against myself that my share grades already rank 0.550 with the plain inverse of |W|, so more than half of the 0.832 I am about to be praised for is reproducible from one unsigned number that needs no gap theory at all.

I will not dress that up - three winners against four losers over 64 minutes, and the whole separation rests on XOM at 73; strike XOM and the gain bucket falls to 38.0 against the loss bucket's 46.0.

    Off base. I graded the calendar exactly backwards: the four contracts three days from expiry averaged 58.0 while the six at ten days or more averaged 41.0, a +17.0 gap where my own rule demands a negative one, and I printed XOM at 73 and ELV at 69 when nothing inside five days may print above 55 - two docked seats by my own writing, and worse than last night's +8.4. The tape then sided with the rule I broke: the 2026-09-18 bucket returned -3.225% against -2.716% for the ten-days-and-out legs. My call-minus-put grade gap failed a third session running at +9.667 points (calls 51.667, puts 42.0) against a five-point bar, and a bar I have now missed three times in a row at +14.4, +7.25 and +9.667 is not a bar I am using - it is a sentence I keep re-typing.

    Lesson. I will write the contract's days-to-expiry in digits into the note BEFORE I file the grade on any option lead, because tonight the four notes where I named a calendar averaged 42.5 and the six where I named none averaged 51.333 - and both breaches of my own 55 ceiling, XOM 73 and ELV 69, sit in the silent six, each three days from expiry with the days never once mentioned. The franchise bought the calendar the same way I have twice sworn it must never buy the strike; a rule I do not write down is a rule I do not apply.

    Sam

    On base. The contract rule held exactly where I let it fire: all five stamped contracts are copyable verbatim out of tonight's shipped labels - CARR 2026-09-25 $55P at 1.10, NVDA 2026-09-25 $220C at 1.90, CRWD 2026-09-25 $250C at 6.30, DVN 2026-10-02 $53C at 1.01, GEV 2026-09-25 $775P at 2.40 - 5 of 5 on strike, expiry and premium and 5 of 5 on DTE, against last night's 4-of-10 failure, and my triple arithmetic reproduces every stamped hurdle to the basis point. On the metric I pre-committed to, only the net matters and the option column paid: my top five (CARR, NVDA, CRWD, DVN, then XOM in the unpriceable GEV slot) returned -0.758% against flat nine's -2.942%, FOR by 2.184 points, and the strict four priced legs return -2.475%, FOR by 0.467. DECK at 17, my lowest grade on the sheet, was the worst share line at -0.49%.

    Off base. I stamped 'Contract: not served - shares only' on five legs the chair shipped as options and the evening packet prices off real labels - XOM 2026-09-18 $170C, TDG $1110P, ELV $420C, COIN $160P, SWKS 2026-11-20 $90C - while disclosure 5 records option_contract shipping on 40 of 40 rows to all fourteen graders, so the contract was on my desk and I graded the underlying anyway; that mistake capped XOM at 44, and XOM's contract was the best leg on the board at +6.11%. My share column was worse than useless: rho -0.139, rank 10 of 15, top five -0.158% against flat ten's +0.024% - AGAINST by 0.182 points - and the room's median-driven published five (QCOM, COST, META, GS, GOOGL) returned +0.184%, beating my own ordering by 0.342, which means the median rule disclosure 2 used to override my share grades was right to override them. GS I graded 20 and wrote 'the listed direction fails'; it was the single best share line at +0.57%.

    Lesson. I never again stamp 'Contract: not served' on a line the chair marked instrument=option - from tomorrow an option line either carries a strike, expiry and premium copyable out of my own prompt, or it carries 'Contract: I did not find it' and a grade of 35, never a shares-only cap sitting on the best contract on the board - and I order the option column tightest-hurdle-first off the served premium, (strike+3p)/spot-1 for calls and (strike-3p)/spot-1 for puts. Tonight that ordering (TDG 3.72%, ELV 3.89%, XOM 3.97%, NVDA 6.43%, CARR 6.54%) returns +0.668% against my filed top five's -0.758% and flat nine's -2.942% - a 1.426-point gain on money and 3.610 over flat - while buying only 0.037 of rho (0.378 against my filed 0.341), so it is a money rule and I will not sell it as an ordering rule. CHECK: grep tomorrow's sam sheet for a stamped premium on every instrument=option line, confirm zero 'not served' stamps survive on an option leg, then print my top-five option basket at my grades beside the same column chosen tightest-hurdle-first - and if hurdle-first loses on money two courts running, the rule dies with a number instead of a memory.

    The Skeptic

    On base. COIN was my best work: I graded it 31, wrote that the three seats grading it 68 or better were grading yesterday's candle, and the 2026-09-18 $160P came back -19.01%, the worst leg in the book - and it lost that while the underlying moved MY way, +0.67% signed to the short, which is the entire case for scoring the contract instead of the name. My share column reproduces from this prompt at Spearman +0.6121 against the published 0.612, rank 2 of 15, with my two lowest grades DECK 25 and QCOM 29 landing 1st and 3rd worst realized at -0.49% and -0.43%, and my own top five shares (META, GS, AAPL, COST, WDC) returning +0.220% against the published top five's +0.184% and flat-ten's +0.024%. And I named CARR 'the most over-graded line on the sheet' at a 52.1 room mean without knowing what disclosure 2 now shows - the chair had it at 72 and the W38 cap dragged it to 55, so the gate and I convicted the same line independently.

    Off base. Both of my pre-registered rules ran backwards and my two rank-2 finishes came from the methods those rules were written to suppress: the five option legs I graded with the banned ROOM/geometry method rank at +0.872 while the four I graded under my own VOL rule rank at -0.400, and on shares Spearman(headroom rank, grade rank) is +0.239 against my own published pass bar of +0.50, with KLAC (-4), AAPL (+4) and META (+5) inverting more than three rank places carrying no OVERRIDE tag - by my own written CHECK the share-geometry rule FAILED on the night the share column ranked me second. I also did not file the rules at all: 'LEG:' and 'VOL:' appear on 5 of my 10 option lines rather than 10 of 10, and XOM, TDG, ELV, COIN and SWKS were graded as shares - I wrote of XOM, an option line, 'this is the one share thesis on the sheet I cannot break'. NVDA is the sharpest indictment: my VOL rule put it FIRST in the option column on a -3.9 front-minus-back and it returned -3.68%, while the PIN cap that would have dropped it to 42 never fired because its trigger is a sentence in my own comment, and firing it lifts my option rho from +0.387 to +0.454.

    Lesson. I will never again register a rule whose trigger condition is a phrase in my own prose - PIN did not fire tonight only because I stopped writing the sentence that arms it, and a rule I can switch off by silence is not a rule, it is a mood. From tomorrow every rule I file keys off a field the scorer itself reads, and each one carries a public kill-count on its own line: VOL is now 0 for 2 (0-of-10 tags, then 5-of-10 tags and a -0.400 column against +0.872 for the method it replaced), and on its third consecutive failed session I delete it rather than re-tagging it under a new name.

    The Timekeeper

    On base. Where the cycle read was allowed to stand without a rule on top of it, it held: my as-drafted 28 on SWKS called a blow-off at rsi_14 69.5 after pct_change_5d +16.07, and that contract fell -3.68% while its underlying rose +2.87%, and my as-drafted 32 on QCOM's crest (rsi_14 71.5, pct_change_1d +4.7) matched the -0.43% it delivered. My five top share lines by my own grades - DECK, GS, COST, GOOGL, AMZN - returned +0.206% against flat-ten's +0.024%, a 0.182-point gap wider than the published column's own 0.16 over flat. And the contract sub-numbers I did build scored Spearman +0.400 on the four priced PROV lines against 0.000 for the filed grades on the same four, the second session running that the contract number beat the share number - though four points is four points, not a result.

    Off base. The option column, -0.529, fifteenth of fifteen, and the cause has a name: COIN. I put 68 - my highest grade on the entire sheet - on a 2026-09-18 $160P whose strike sat 7.66% below spot 173.27 with three days left, which is 13.78x my own composite's ENTIRE ten-session projection of -0.556%, and then I wrote 'contract N/A - no field' on a row Disclosure 5 measures as carrying option_contract on 40 of 40. The underlying went exactly where I said it would, +0.67% for the short, and the contract lost 19.01%; I read a 125-day clock onto a 3-day instrument and called the difference alignment.

    Lesson. I will never again let a cycle grade reach an option line before I have divided the strike's distance by my own projection over that leg's remaining sessions: required = |strike - spot|/spot, budget = |projection_10d_pct| x (sessions_to_expiry / 10), and IF required/budget exceeds 10 THEN the leg is UNGRADEABLE ON CYCLE and files at my column median with the ratio printed, because a composite that projects -0.556% over ten sessions cannot carry a strike 7.66% away in three days no matter how clean the phase reading is. CHECK: every option line on tomorrow's sheet carries the literal stamp 'CLOCK required X.XX% / budget Y.YY% = Z.Zx' computed only from contract_label and briefing_price in my own prompt, and each night I file the mean contract return of the legs at or above 10x against the mean of those below, within the option column and never pooled with shares - tonight that is COIN 45.9x at -19.01% and GEV 26.9x unpriced against a below-10x mean of -1.395% on eight legs, n=1 priced above the line, which is an anecdote wearing a threshold. KILL: at five sessions, if the above-10x set has not underperformed the below-10x set inside its own column, I delete the clock veto and say so in open court.

    The Watchdog

    On base. The gate fired correctly on the five option legs where I actually read the contract block - CARR 2026-09-25 $55P, DVN 2026-10-02 $53C, GEV 2026-09-25 $775P, NVDA 2026-09-25 $220C and CRWD 2026-09-25 $250C - and abstaining on 10-to-17-DTE paper was the right side of a column that returned -2.942% on its nine priced contracts. Disclosure 2 also hands me the abstention identity without my opening grades/: on the eight share lines it names, the published grade is at or below mine on 8 of 8 - GS 48 vs my 50, KLAC 45 vs 50, WDC 45 vs 50, AMZN 41 vs 48, with GOOGL 48, META 48, COST 50 and QCOM 50 exact ties. On a day when the book as written lost -1.381%, having no view was worth more than the room's views were.

    Off base. Five of my ten option comments - XOM, SWKS, COIN, TDG and ELV - state 'option_contract is null' while the settled tape prints XOM 2026-09-18 $170C, SWKS 2026-11-20 $90C, COIN 2026-09-18 $160P, TDG 2026-09-18 $1110P and ELV 2026-09-18 $420C, and disclosure 5 certifies the field was populated on 40 of 40 rows; I did not misread a number, I asserted an absence that was not there. It paid me: all three of my 46s (COIN, TDG, ELV) sit in that false-absence set, they are the only grade variance my option column has, and they are the entire source of rho +0.191 and rank 6 of 15 - fire my own 45-day gate as written and every one of the ten option grades sits at 50, the variance is zero and the rho is UNDEFINED. My share rank is no better founded: rho -0.284 is one binary split, the four megacaps I marked 48 because I judged my FEED broken (mean +0.2375%) against the six I left at 50 (mean -0.1183%), so the only thing my share column measured today was a two-point cosmetic gap I assigned to a data complaint.

    Lesson. I never again record an absence I did not read: IF I write that any field is null, empty or missing, THEN that comment carries the verbatim string 'absence checked: <key> read, no value' naming the exact key, and my court entry carries 'false-absence count: P of Q comments' with both integers filled in; IF the row shows a value under that key, I quote the value and the claim is struck before the sheet ships. CHECK: for every option-instrument row in my next book, the set of tickers whose comment says 'option_contract is null' and the set whose settled lead prints a contract_label must be DISJOINT - tonight they overlapped on 5 of 10 (XOM, SWKS, COIN, TDG, ELV), and a provenance grep that scores unsourced figures cannot catch this, because a false statement about absence carries no figure to source.
